intro.title: Children Prop
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that accepts and displays content passed from a parent component using the children prop concept. You will learn how to use content projection with Angular's <ng-content> directive to create flexible, reusable components. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript, and template syntax. By the end, you'll understand how to pass and render dynamic content within your components.
intro.usecase: The children prop pattern is fundamental in Angular for creating reusable, composable UI components that appear in nearly every real-world application. You'll use this when building dashboard layouts where cards, charts, and widgets need consistent containers, or when creating modal dialogs that can display any type of content. This pattern enables developers to create flexible navigation menus that can contain links, dropdowns, or icons, and form components that wrap input fields with consistent styling and validation. Mastering children props allows you to build maintainable component libraries where parent components define structure while child components provide customizable content.
